manuscript_quote: (protocol) the audit and the behavioural readout use the same edit
actual_intervention: one hook implementation; rank-1 projection at every token of the demographic span, prefill only, every decoder layer, sequential source state; identity checks (alpha 0, rank 0, non-span positions untouched) pass exactly on all four models
supporting_output: pilot_per_item.parquet (24 dev seeds per model, 5 conditions)
metric_formula: mean |C| and generation validity per condition, chat format, demographic pairs
interval: Llama-3.1-8B: unedited 0.141 -> span edit 0.110, last-token edit 0.168; validity 0.88 / 0.96 / 0.88; Qwen2.5-7B: unedited 0.761 -> span edit 0.639, last-token edit 0.646; validity 0.96 / 0.92 / 1.00; Gemma-2-2B: unedited 0.758 -> span edit 0.536, last-token edit 0.772; validity 0.88 / 0.79 / 0.58; Phi-4-mini: unedited 0.359 -> span edit 0.237, last-token edit 0.651; validity 0.92 / 0.96 / 0.33
permitted_wording: The matched-position edit reduces mean |C| on every model with no loss of output validity. The legacy last-token edit raises |C| on Phi and Llama and collapses Phi's output validity to a third: a large part of the original 'damage' is output invalidity under a position-transferred edit, not accuracy loss.
note: Identity pairs give |C| = 0 exactly under the sequential convention; the frozen (legacy TransformerLens) source state gives up to 0.30, 1.18, 1.81, 0.75 on identity pairs, so it is not a null instrument.

manuscript_quote: the erasure removes X per cent of the targeted signal
location: P2 test phase, results/v2/p2_confirmatory.csv (C1, C3), p2_summary.csv
actual_intervention: rank-1 centred-SVD projection at the demographic span, prefill only, every layer, alpha 1; 160 test seeds per model, fit on the FIT split only, mask-clean pairs
metric_formula: D = mean over seeds of (|C_pre| - |C_post|), seed-cluster bootstrap 95%% CI; R = 1 - mean|C_post| / mean|C_pre|; Holm over the four confirmatory comparisons
permitted_wording: The matched-position erasure lowers the demographic dependence on all four models, by an amount whose Holm-corrected interval excludes zero on Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.1-8B and Phi-4-mini and on Qwen2.5-7B at the uncorrected level only; rank-matched random subspaces remove nothing. Report D with its interval and R as the secondary normalised statistic; never the win rate.
note: The shipped 'removed' quantity was the win rate W = mean(|C_post| < |C_pre|); its test-phase value for the erasure is 0.54, 0.54, 0.59, 0.50, i.e. the null value, so it must not appear as a result.

actual_intervention: same edit at ranks 1, 2, 4 (exploratory beyond rank 1)
permitted_wording: Higher rank removes more on three of four models with no accuracy cost; state that ranks 2 and 4 are exploratory (the confirmatory comparisons are at rank 1).

manuscript_quote: Task accuracy falls by 0.16 to 0.58, and the rate at which answers flip ... rises
actual_intervention: same edit; canonical option mapping of the generated answer (identity mapped through the swap); attempted denominator; invalid outputs counted as failures
metric_formula: paired change in generation accuracy over seeds, bootstrap CI, Holm
interval: Llama-3.1-8B: generation accuracy change +0.025 [-0.003, +0.053], Holm p = 0.086; validity 0.99 -> 0.98 | Qwen2.5-7B: generation accuracy change +0.022 [-0.013, +0.056], Holm p = 0.376; validity 0.94 -> 0.96 | Gemma-2-2B: generation accuracy change +0.072 [+0.028, +0.119], Holm p = 0.002 REJECT; validity 0.93 -> 0.93 | Phi-4-mini: generation accuracy change +0.037 [-0.000, +0.078], Holm p = 0.144; validity 0.98 -> 0.99
permitted_wording: Under the matched-position edit generation accuracy does not fall on any model; it rises on Gemma-2-2B with a Holm-corrected interval excluding zero and is unchanged within its interval on the other three. The original accuracy losses must not be reported.

actual_intervention: official concept-erasure LEACE applied as its exact affine map at the span (frozen fit, and sequential concept scrubbing); random orthonormal subspaces of matched rank; neutral-contrast basis; mean-difference direction
permitted_wording: At the demographic span, faithful LEACE under either fitting protocol, random subspaces, the neutral-contrast basis and the mean-difference direction all leave the commutator essentially unchanged; the erasure's effect is specific to the intervention-selected direction.

manuscript_quote: (external capability under a GLOBAL application policy)
location: P2 test, p2_capability.parquet (capability_policy = all, site = all)
actual_intervention: the SAME bases applied at EVERY token position (prefill and decoding) on 200 MMLU test questions and 20,000 WikiText-2 tokens, because external prompts have no demographic span
metric_formula: MMLU accuracy (option log-likelihood, n = 200); WikiText-2 perplexity over 20k tokens in 1024-token windows; single deterministic pass
permitted_wording: Applied everywhere, the same direction is destructive: MMLU falls and perplexity rises by orders of magnitude on Phi-4-mini and Gemma-2-2B, less on Qwen2.5-7B, least on Llama-3.1-8B; random subspaces applied everywhere change neither. Faithful LEACE applied everywhere is mild. State this as the resolution of the original finding: the damage is a property of the application site, not of the direction.
note: No interval: one deterministic pass per probe.

actual_intervention: targeted edit vs random subspace with strength matched to the same removed activation energy on dev, frozen for test
metric_formula: option-scoring accuracy loss and |C| change vs unedited, seed-cluster bootstrap
interval: Llama-3.1-8B: targeted |C| change -0.044 [-0.072, -0.019], accuracy loss -0.152 [-0.203, -0.105]; energy-matched random |C| change -0.003 [-0.015, +0.009], accuracy loss +0.003 [-0.006, +0.016] | Qwen2.5-7B: targeted |C| change -0.076 [-0.146, -0.004], accuracy loss -0.019 [-0.060, +0.022]; energy-matched random |C| change -0.012 [-0.037, +0.013], accuracy loss +0.009 [-0.009, +0.028] | Gemma-2-2B: targeted |C| change -0.114 [-0.186, -0.044], accuracy loss -0.133 [-0.186, -0.083]; energy-matched random |C| change +0.006 [-0.025, +0.038], accuracy loss -0.006 [-0.016, -0.000] | Phi-4-mini: targeted |C| change -0.113 [-0.163, -0.059], accuracy loss -0.098 [-0.147, -0.054]; energy-matched random |C| change +0.002 [-0.025, +0.031], accuracy loss +0.003 [-0.016, +0.022]
permitted_wording: An energy-matched random subspace neither reduces |C| nor changes accuracy, so the effect is not a generic perturbation-size effect. Negative 'accuracy loss' is a gain: option-scoring accuracy rises under the targeted edit on three models.

actual_intervention: bases fitted on unedited activations (frozen) vs refitted layer by layer on already-edited activations (sequential); early / middle / late blocks as diagnostics
permitted_wording: Sequential refitting removes the same amount of dependence; the accuracy gain is smaller under sequential fitting. There is no harm for either protocol to explain.

manuscript_quote: the audited direction lies along hidden dimensions holding massive activations ... consistent with the damage
actual_intervention: massive coordinates identified on neutral calibration prompts (mean |activation| and input stability); after erasure the removed component is restored on those coordinates only, with random-coordinate and equal-energy restoration controls
interval: Llama-3.1-8B: erased |C| change -0.044 [-0.072, -0.019], accuracy loss -0.152 [-0.203, -0.105]; massive coordinates restored: -0.043 [-0.071, -0.016], -0.155 [-0.208, -0.108]; restore-all identity check -0.009 [-0.020, +0.002] | Qwen2.5-7B: erased |C| change -0.076 [-0.146, -0.004], accuracy loss -0.019 [-0.060, +0.022]; massive coordinates restored: -0.085 [-0.156, -0.015], -0.025 [-0.066, +0.016]; restore-all identity check +0.007 [-0.016, +0.029] | Gemma-2-2B: erased |C| change -0.114 [-0.186, -0.044], accuracy loss -0.133 [-0.186, -0.083]; massive coordinates restored: -0.136 [-0.210, -0.063], -0.130 [-0.184, -0.075]; restore-all identity check +0.006 [-0.024, +0.035] | Phi-4-mini: erased |C| change -0.113 [-0.163, -0.059], accuracy loss -0.098 [-0.147, -0.054]; massive coordinates restored: -0.127 [-0.180, -0.069], -0.085 [-0.133, -0.041]; restore-all identity check +0.003 [-0.022, +0.029]
permitted_wording: Restoring the massive-activation coordinates after erasure leaves both the |C| reduction and the accuracy change unchanged, so those coordinates carry no part of the effect at the demographic span. The massive-activation explanation of the original paper is not supported and must not be claimed; coordinate overlap may be reported as descriptive only.

manuscript_quote: The damage can be anticipated: the audit score alone separates the items erasure cannot repair, AUC 0.85 to 0.93
actual_intervention: per-prompt forecast of NEW generation errors after the frozen edit (rank 1, alpha 1) among prompts the unedited model answered correctly; GroupKFold on DEV seeds, one evaluation on TEST seeds; predictors: base rate, pre-edit margin/entropy/benchmark/length, audit score alone, baseline plus audit
metric_formula: AUROC; paired seed-cluster bootstrap of the AUROC difference, 95%% interval
eligible_n: TEST prompts initially correct, per model
interval: Llama-3.1-8B: AUROC(baseline+audit) - AUROC(baseline) = +0.001 [-0.061, +0.056]; audit-only AUROC 0.506, baseline AUROC 0.654, prevalence 0.042 | Qwen2.5-7B: AUROC(baseline+audit) - AUROC(baseline) = +0.002 [-0.010, +0.011]; audit-only AUROC 0.622, baseline AUROC 0.733, prevalence 0.051 | Gemma-2-2B: AUROC(baseline+audit) - AUROC(baseline) = +0.002 [+0.000, +0.006]; audit-only AUROC 0.622, baseline AUROC 0.648, prevalence 0.068 | Phi-4-mini: AUROC(baseline+audit) - AUROC(baseline) = -0.009 [-0.024, +0.001]; audit-only AUROC 0.570, baseline AUROC 0.704, prevalence 0.036
permitted_wording: The audit score adds no held-out prediction of post-edit errors beyond a cheap confidence-and-length baseline on any model. The forecast contribution is removed; the original AUC values were the separation of an audit-defined target from itself and must not be reported.
